root_cause.text: The `rto_next_cpu()` function in the real-time scheduler load balancing logic did not verify whether the selected target CPU was the currently executing CPU, allowing an overloaded CPU to repeatedly select itself and trigger an infinite self-IPI loop.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `int this_cpu = smp_processor_id();` and a conditional `if (cpu == this_cpu) continue;` within `rto_next_cpu()` to skip the local CPU, and the CVE description notes that without this filter, "CPU0... gets reselected, causing CPU0 to queue irq_work to itself and send self-IPIs repeatedly."

intent_record.intent_summary: Corrects rto_next_cpu logic to exclude the current CPU from selection to prevent self-directed IPIs.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check within the rto_next_cpu function loop that compares the candidate CPU with this_cpu, skipping the iteration if they match.
intent_record.how: Prevents the function from selecting the local CPU, ensuring that subsequent operations target a different processor and avoiding sending Inter-Processor Interrupts to itself.
